07.10.2024 Order No.

This is an application under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
2.

The petitioner is an accused in connection with S.T. Case No.58 of 2023 arising out of G.R. Case No.116 of 2023 corresponding to Anandapur P.S. Case No.116 of 2023 for the offences under Sections 376(2)(n)/379/507/506/420 of I.P.C. read with Sections 66-E/67/67(A) of the I.T. Act pending in the Court of the learned S.D.J.M., Anandapur.
The petitioner had approached before the learned Court below praying for grant of bail.
The learned Court below vide its order dated 11.09.2023 has rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.
4.

The prosecution case in short is that, on 13.06.2023, informant/victim lodged a written report alleging therein that the petitioner has kept forcible physical relationship with her for several times since last 4 to 5 months by giving false promise to provide a job to her.

It is alleged that the petitioner had taken cash of Rs.1,40,000/- and gold necklace weighing about 13 grams from her for giving the job and he usually called her to Bhubaneswar, where he sexually assaulted her.
When the victim did not get any job and requested the petitioner to return her money and gold necklace, the petitioner made viral her private photos in social media.

sentences.text: The victim, who is stated to be 29 years of age has been examined as P.W.2.
Perusal of the evidence adduced by the prosecution particularly the evidence of the victim reveals that the petitioner, who is 32 years old has been in relationship with the victim.
They were staying in Bhubaneswar and Bangalore.
During their stay, they had sexual relationship.
There was some money transaction between them.

It appears from the cross-examination of the victim that at times,
she has also taken money from the petitioner and vice-versa.
It has also come on record through the evidence that the photographs and videos recorded by the petitioner were sent to the victim in the Email.
However, nothing is illuminating on the record that as to whether those photographs and videos were viral in the social media.
However, on the contrary, the evidence is otherwise.

6. Regard being had to the period of custody from 06.07.2023, the nature of accusation and the fact that the evidence of the witnesses have already been recorded by the prosecution particularly the evidence of the victim, I am inclined to admit the petitioner on bail.

Hence, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail by the Court in seisin over the matter in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper, subject to the following additional conditions:-
(i) The petitioner shall appear before the trial Court on each date of hearing without fail and seek unnecessary adjournment.
(ii) He shall not tamper with the evidence in any manner whatsoever.
(iii) He shall not keep contact with the victim and her family members in any manner whatsoever.

In the event, the petitioner is found wanting for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
7. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.

(S.S. Mishra) Judge Swarna Location: High Court of Orissa Kuna Biswal vs State Of Odisha .... Opposite Party(S) on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192826439/
